p4_card.identity: Apinocaltamide (ACT-709478, NBI-827104), a small-molecule triple T-type calcium channel blocker (CACNA1G, CACNA1H, CACNA1I). Catalogue identity: CHEMBL4217292 (ChEMBL_37 curated mechanism: 'Voltage-gated T-type calcium channel blocker'; max phase 2; no approval statement in any source used); a DGIdb-only record (CAT:DGIDB:b811c040b8a4) repeats the same three targets from the same ChEMBL claim and is not an independent confirmation.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only as a mechanistic discriminator of the ethosuximide result in the Wwox-null mouse (need NEED-T-TYPE-CALCIUM). Not an indication, not a treatment proposal. The sources are healthy volunteers (age not stated in the abstracts; the indexing terms include adolescents and young adults) and rodent seizure models of unstated age; nothing is known in a developing brain or in any Wwox system.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA in the repository: no record, card or claim names apinocaltamide. It entered through the reverse path (compound -> targets -> needs), not from a paper on WWOX. Not 'never tried': no search beyond PubMed titles and the catalogue was run.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: EB-ETX-01 (ethosuximide, same need), DL-MECH-170, map record N-03; need NEED-T-TYPE-CALCIUM.
p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. If it reproduces the ethosuximide pattern it would support T-type dependence of the provoked seizure; if not, it would make the ethosuximide result less likely to be T-type mediated. Neither outcome says anything about benefit in WWOX-DEE.
p4_card.mechanism: Block of Cav3.1, Cav3.2 and Cav3.3 (the abstracts call it selective and highly potent with 'no relevant activity on other targets'; that is the sponsor's statement, not an independent selectivity panel). Quantitative record re-examined in IT5 (pharmacology_it5_20261029/ttype_cav3_h01.tsv): in the one sponsor discovery paper the flux IC50 is in the low nanomolar range at all three human isoforms (a span of under three-fold) and at the rat, mouse and dog orthologues, with an L-type Cav1.2 flux IC50 in the micromolar range (a margin of roughly 130 to 380-fold, one assay, one laboratory); patch-clamp affinity for the inactivated state of Cav3.3 is about 75-fold higher than for the resting state, so effective potency depends on membrane potential and on the age-dependent resting potential of the neurons. Ethosuximide is in a different regime: sub-millimolar to millimolar, state dependent, abstract-level for the cloned human channels and a persistent-current figure only (the lower inactivated-state constants in that abstract belong to a methsuximide metabolite, not ethosuximide), a flux IC50 above the top of a five-millimolar screen for Cav3.3 in one assay, and no concentration of it was measured in the Wwox pups. A concordant apinocaltamide result therefore tests the T-type reading across a nominal potency gap of about four and a half to five orders of magnitude against the persistent-current figure and at least five and a half against the flux bound (the endpoints differ, patch-clamp persistent current against calcium flux), with brain exposure of both drugs the open variable. Wanted direction: T-type current down (need direction 'down', coupling 'same').

external_not_wwox_evidence: ChEMBL_37 mechanism row CHEMBL4217292 (reference ids PubMed 29116786, PubMed 31004346)
PubMed abstracts 29116786, 31004346, 31994022, 40165594, 38605177 (abstract level; none carries a receipt)

for: Ethosuximide is the only drug that suppressed the late phase of the provoked seizure score in the null mouse and not (significantly) in wild type or heterozygote; apinocaltamide shares the T-type target class (see the premise caveat in 'against').

A structurally unrelated three-subtype blocker, described by the sponsor as brain-penetrant and without relevant off-target activity, lets 'is it the T-type channel' be asked without ethosuximide's other possible actions. Set aside, not excluded: suvecaltamide, Z944, TTA-A2, ML218 (access and independence not established).
Healthy-volunteer tolerability data exist (abstracts of two phase 1 studies; transient mild-to-moderate events including dizziness, somnolence and headache, with an up-titration scheme).
The 2025 rodent abstract positions the compound for childhood absence epilepsy and syndromes with spike-and-wave discharges.
against: Premise: ethosuximide's T-type attribution in the Wwox paper rests on its Methods wording only (needs audit C10), so 'same target class' is not an independent anchor; a concordant result would raise the T-type reading, a discordant one could equally reflect exposure.
Genotype specificity of the ethosuximide result rests on one experiment without an interaction test and a possible floor effect in wild type.

Rodent efficacy is stated for absence-type discharges and generalized convulsive tests (the latter at higher concentration), not for focal-onset seizures; the Wwox model is a pentylenetetrazol-provoked score.
Class-level in vitro signal: T-type blockers lowered embryonic cortical progenitor viability (other compounds, rat E14); the dependence reported there was on Cav3.1, which apinocaltamide also blocks.

Sponsor-derived sources: the discovery, phase 1 and rodent abstracts are sponsor-affiliated and the ChEMBL mechanism references are sponsor-linked; the only non-sponsor source is the cryo-EM structure of human Cav3.2 (direct pore block of one subtype; nothing on Cav3.1/Cav3.3 or on exposure in vivo). No independent replication is read.
Multiple-dose abstract: a tolerability signal in the first cohort forced a dose reduction before the up-titration scheme.

Pharmacokinetics (abstract level): slow absorption and a half-life of well over a day in adults, against a one-hour PTZ late phase in a pup; the timing and exposure in a Wwox-null pup (a sick animal with possible weight and glucose confounds on disposition) are unknown.
The catalogue holds no potency or exposure.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Species (rat, mouse, human adult), age (pup versus adult), seizure type and provoking agent all differ from the Wwox-null pup.

p4_card.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. ChEMBL records a clinical-candidate statement only; how a research supply could be obtained is not established here and no contact was made.
p4_card.pharmacology: Triple T-type blocker; abstract-level human pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers (slow absorption and a long half-life are reported); multiple-dose tolerability reported with an up-titration scheme. No pup or brain-exposure datum. Doses and concentrations are deliberately not reproduced.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Not assessed. A weak gastrointestinal CYP3A4 induction signal is reported in the multiple-dose abstract; interaction with valproate is reported as synergistic in a mouse test (abstract).

question_history: need NEED-T-TYPE-CALCIUM; reverse search 'compound apinocaltamide' (2026-10-28, closed-loop case a)
p4_card.predictions: Registered before any such experiment: if the late-phase suppression in the null is T-type mediated, a structurally unrelated T-type blocker at a brain-relevant exposure should reduce it in the null and at most weakly in wild type and heterozygote; if the suppression is not reproduced at confirmed exposure, the ethosuximide result is not supported as T-type mediated. A negative result at an unconfirmed exposure refutes nothing.
p4_card.next_measurement: In the Wwox-/- preweaning pup, a same-day concurrent PTZ-alone control in all three genotypes, ethosuximide and apinocaltamide as separate arms with plasma and brain exposure measured, blind scoring, and a drug-by-genotype interaction test planned in advance; discriminating result: both T-type blockers reduce the late phase specifically in the null (interaction supported), against ethosuximide-only reduction (off-target or non-specific) or reduction in all genotypes (a general antiseizure effect, as with lithium).
p4_card.value_added: A new compound reached from the catalogue with no card; adds a mechanism-level discriminator for the only drug result in the need, carries the class-level developing-cortex caution from the repository's own reading, and states that the sources are abstract-level.
p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.
